_comment: WC2026 Round of 32. KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Routes: Argentina WON Group J with a PERFECT nine (3-0 Algeria, 2-0 Austria, 3-1 Jordan; 9 pts, GF 8 GA 1, rating 95) -- tournament top-tier, dominant, relentless attack, solid at the back. Cape Verde qualified as a BEST THIRD from Group H (0-0 Spain, 2-2 Uruguay, 0-0 Saudi Arabia; 3 pts on THREE DRAWS, GF 2 GA 2, GD 0, rating 58) -- a genuine minnow by rating but a PROVEN DEEP LOW BLOCK: they held SPAIN to 0-0 and Saudi to 0-0, scoring only vs Uruguay. Class gap is ENORMOUS (~37, 95 vs 58) -> Argentina a heavy favourite. KEY tension: unlike Spain-Austria (open/leaky underdog -> rout), Cape Verde is the OPPOSITE archetype -- an organized block that frustrated Spain to 0-0. So this is NOT a guaranteed rout: Argentina should WIN, but the SHAPE is more likely a controlled low-to-moderate-margin win (1-0/2-0) than a 4-0 blowout, because Cape Verde defends deep and barely attacks. There is a real (if modest) frustration/0-0 tail given the block -- the 'favourite vs proven low block' pattern (Cape Verde 0-0 Spain is literally in that list). KNOCKOUT CAUTION APPLIED: Cape Verde's lambda kept very low (they rarely score), so BTTS-No ~65%, Argentina clean sheet ~62% -- do NOT lean both-score. RECAL: first pass sat 4.8 pts BELOW the market on Argentina (73.8 vs 78.6) -- applied the Spain lesson (do NOT fade an elite favourite) and lifted Argentina 2.10 -> 2.38 / trimmed Cape Verde 0.52 -> 0.48 to align, while keeping the goals texture cautious. Home = Argentina (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.result: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde after extra time (1-1 at 90'). The heavy favourite advances to the Round of 16 (where they meet Egypt), but Cape Verde -- the proven low block -- took them all the way to extra time and SCORED TWICE. A five-goal scare.

_postmatch.verdict: Right on the DELIVERABLE, wrong on the TEXTURE -- and the texture miss is the lesson. Argentina advanced as the 90.3% pick (a ✅ on who goes through), and the tie reaching extra time is the model's 15.4% draw-at-90' / ET branch landing. But almost everything about the SHAPE went against the forecast: I predicted a controlled low-margin win (2-0 modal, Argentina clean sheet 62%, Cape Verde BTTS-No 65%, CV lambda just 0.48) -- instead Cape Verde held Argentina 1-1 through 90' AND scored TWICE in a 3-2 thriller. Two of my calibration choices bit here: (1) the SPAIN-lesson alignment UP -- I lifted Argentina 73.8 -> 79.3 and TRIMMED the draw 19% -> 15.4%, fading Cape Verde's block; but Cape Verde is a PROVEN elite low block (0-0 vs Spain) and it did it again (1-1 vs Argentina to 90'), so the block's deep/draw tail deserved MORE weight, not less. (2) the KNOCKOUT-CAUTION trim of the underdog's attack drove Cape Verde's scoring toward zero (BTTS-No 65%); they scored two. Honest read: the advancement number was correct and Argentina's class told in the end (extra time, where the minnow tired), but I was over-confident on the game SHAPE against a side that had already proven it can smother elite attacks.
_postmatch.lesson: Refinement to BOTH standing notes, from the same-day contrast with Egypt: (a) the Spain lesson ('don't fade the elite favourite') is about the ADVANCE probability -- keep aligning THAT up -- but it must NOT flatten the draw/extra-time tail when the underdog is a PROVEN elite low block. Cape Verde (0-0 Spain, 1-1 Argentina-to-90') belongs in the 'favourite vs proven low block' pattern where the draw is worth MORE than it looks; I trimmed that tail and it came in. (b) Knockout caution lowers the GAME's goal expectation but must not drive a specific underdog's scoring to ~zero -- a low block can still nick goals, especially in a tiring extra time (Cape Verde scored two). Net: advancement read good (90%+ favourite advanced), but for a proven-block underdog, keep the deep/draw tail fat and don't zero out their attack. Don't over-update on the win itself -- Argentina DID advance as forecast; the correction is purely to the texture/tail, not the side.
